author: 5kO0
content:
## Bug

proto-blue v0.3.1 (commit e36a5fa) declares `rust-version = "1.85"` in the workspace Cargo.toml but ships seven let-chain expressions stabilized in Rust 1.88 (released 2025-06-26). On a 1.85 toolchain `cargo build` will fail.

## Sites (verified)

- proto-blue-identity/src/did.rs:108-110 (4-arm let-chain in cache-check fast path)
- proto-blue-ws/src/keepalive.rs:242-243 (reconnect-limit guard)
- proto-blue-lexicon/src/validation.rs:315-320 (blob accept-list)
- proto-blue-lexicon/src/validation.rs:327-329 (blob max-size)
- proto-blue-lexicon/src/lexicons.rs:360-363 (query output schema)
- proto-blue-lexicon/src/lexicons.rs:371-372 (procedure input schema)
- proto-blue-lexicon/src/lexicons.rs:376-378 (procedure output schema)

## Why CI didn't catch it

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` pins every job to `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`, which always grabs the latest stable (currently >=1.88). The declared MSRV had no verifier — it was a number in Cargo.toml that nothing enforced.

## Plan (category A, root-cause)

1. Bump `proto-blue/Cargo.toml` line 31 `rust-version = "1.85"` -> `rust-version = "1.88"`. This reflects the truth: the code we shipped requires 1.88.
2. Add an `msrv` job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` pinned to `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.88` running `cargo check --workspace --locked --all-targets`. Prevents future drift.
3. Verify locally with cargo check + clippy + fmt.

## Notes

- Not rewriting let-chains to nested if-lets: the code is clearer as written, and the 1.85 promise was already broken in v0.3.1 so we're documenting reality, not regressing.
- This is arguably a packaging fix (the binary published doesn't compile on its declared MSRV), so a patch release v0.3.2 is defensible. Release decision is for the human; this issue covers only the technical fix.
- The new MSRV job will also implicitly verify that no crate requires anything above 1.88. If it does, that surfaces as a separate finding.
